To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phase-field crystal equation is not derivable from density functional theory and that the phase-field equation is not a good approximation of density functional theory.

fundamental measure theory can serve as a very accurate benchmark, Taylor expansion strongly affects the results, and that the phase-field crystal order parameter is a smeared and rescaled density field.

the Taylor expansion of fundamental measure theory is accurate for the free energies, surface tension, and vacancy concentration of the crystal, whereas the phase-field crystal approximation is not, and that the phase-field crystal free energy is not consistent with the Taylor-expanded free energy.

the phase-field crystal method, in its current state, is not suitable for the study of the thermodynamic properties of hard-sphere fluids.

The main takeaway from our work is that
phase-field crystal models should not be used to study systems where the density varies by more than a factor of two.

the phase-field crystal method is a powerful tool for modeling crystallization processes in systems with short-range interactions, but that its range of validity is more restricted than often assumed.

phase-field crystal models can be derived from density functional theory, but that the resulting models are not as accurate as density functional theory itself, and that the phase-field crystal order parameter is not necessarily a good proxy for the density itself.
